clauses.anchor: CONTRACT.md paragraph 2: "An ordinary Joker acquired by a normal shop Buy contributes +2 to the player's hand limit while owned."
CONTRACT.md paragraph 2: "Ordinary sale removes exactly its own +2."
CONTRACT.md paragraph 2: "Preserve all other active hand-limit contributions, including those acquired before or after it."
clauses.note: before.sell keeps a Juggler bought later; after.sell keeps an earlier Juggler and a later target; second.sell keeps an earlier Juggler.

clauses.anchor: CONTRACT.md paragraph 2: "More than one ordinary physical instance contributes independently; removing one cannot remove another's contribution."
CONTRACT.md paragraph 2: "After a sale the next actual refill/deal obeys the remaining limit."
CONTRACT.md paragraph 3: "Acquisition/removal must happen exactly once per actual instance lifecycle."
CONTRACT.md paragraph 3: "Merely displaying the card, scoring a hand, changing rounds, or observing the shop does not reapply the effect."
clauses.note: No target is owned at observation_stable, real_draw or real_play, so scoring a hand or changing rounds with a target owned is never exercised. While a target is owned, only the eight quiet frames before each transaction snapshot cover shop observation.

clauses.anchor: CONTRACT.md paragraph 3: "After a normal removal a subsequent legal acquisition and removal must still work."
CONTRACT.md paragraph 3: "Do not reset the whole limit to a default or to a snapshot taken before other owners changed it."
CONTRACT.md paragraph 4: "Target registration is mod reversible_hand_limit, prefix rhl, center j_rhl_spacer."
clauses.note: The prepared shop stock must hold j_rhl_spacer; read by the setup case prepared.

clauses.anchor: CONTRACT.md paragraph 4: "Native ordinary Juggler may be another independent hand-limit contributor."
CONTRACT.md paragraph 5: "Do not edit runtime/fixture/observer/tests/dependencies or external files."
clauses.note: Enforced when the submission is sealed (plugins/balatro/src/rhenium_balatro/submission.py:32-47), not by a case.

known_issues: Cascading failures: each transaction compares the absolute hand limit (tasks/reversible_hand_limit/v1/private/scenario.py:68-72), so one wrong sale at before.sell also fails the eight later target cases. The starter and M03-snapshot-restore have the same failure vector, so the number of failed target cases does not count defects.
